does: Cuts away what will not be eaten or will not cook well: sinew, surplus fat, tough leaves, stalks and ragged edges.

intro.what: Trimming removes tough or unwanted parts while keeping useful food.
intro.why: It teaches you to follow the boundary between what should be removed and what should remain.
intro.idea: Remove carefully, keep the good part

how: Slide the tip of the knife under a strip of sinew, angle the blade up against it and draw the knife along, so that the sinew comes away with almost no meat.
Leave a thin, even layer of fat on a joint that will be roasted.
Snap or cut the ends off beans, and pull away any string.
For an artichoke, break off the stalk, pull away the dark outer leaves, cut off the top, pare the base smooth and scoop out the hairy choke. Rub every cut with lemon at once.
Keep meat trimmings for a stock or for rendering.

cues.text: Clean, even surfaces with no silvery skin, no ragged flaps and no dark outer leaves.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting deep and wasting good flesh along with the sinew.
mistakes.fix: Keep the blade angled up against what you are taking off.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving a cut artichoke in the air, where it turns brown within moments.
mistakes.fix: Rub each cut with lemon, or drop the trimmed artichoke into water sharpened with lemon.

quiz.question: What is the aim of trimming sinew from meat?
choices: Cut away a thick layer of meat with every strip.
Leave ragged sinew attached for easier slicing.
Remove the tough layer with little useful flesh.
quiz.because: Following the sinew closely avoids wasting flesh while removing a tough part.

quiz.question: How should the blade angle when removing sinew?
choices: Up against the sinew being removed.
Flat across a thick slice of flesh.
quiz.because: An upward angle follows the unwanted layer instead of cutting deeply into useful meat.

quiz.question: Which surface suggests careful trimming?
choices: Clean and even without silvery skin or ragged flaps.
Tough outer leaves still attached everywhere.
quiz.because: A clean surface shows unwanted parts removed without unnecessary damage.

quiz.question: A cut artichoke browns while you work. What should change?
choices: Leave all cuts exposed until trimming is finished.
Dry the cut surfaces in warm air.
Rub cuts with lemon promptly or use lemon-sharpened water.
quiz.because: Protecting the freshly exposed surfaces limits their rapid browning.
